title: The Future Economics of Defense Aviation (Are We in a Defense Tech Bubble?)
key_claim: BCG, with Vertical Research Partners, finds that exquisite platforms typically derive about half of their lifetime profit from sustainment, over $10 billion for the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet across a $20.3 billion lifetime programme, while expendable systems generate nearly all their value at initial production.
frame_summary: This source argues that the durable profit in defence aviation still sits with legacy platforms because sustainment revenue is annuity-like and survives budget drawdowns, so primes and investors should treat low-cost entrants as a portfolio addition rather than a replacement for the core.
verbatim_quote: Exquisite platforms typically derive about half of their lifetime profit from sustainment (over $10 billion for the Super Hornet across a $20.3 billion lifetime program).
verbatim_list: In exquisite programs, Tier 1 suppliers—particularly suppliers of major components like engines, mission and communication systems, and sensors—can capture 40% to 50% of lifecycle profits independently of the platform prime.
